title: Prove Venus as a thin native client for Orbit
description: Prove the smallest useful native graphical materializer for one accepted Orbit session while preserving Orbit as the sole PTY and terminal authority. The initial experiment is one local Linux window, one active client, exact Orbit contract consumption, and no workspace feature expansion.
design: Orbit remains the active implementation frontier until orb-9o6 closes and the user explicitly activates Venus. Venus consumes accepted ORB-C4, ORB-C5, and ORB-C6 behavior, preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C3 and ORB-C7 by remaining transient and non-authoritative, and proves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 in this repository. First choose a backend and composition shape through the evidence and crate gates; then implement one bounded vertical slice against an exact Orbit revision. Graphical code never enters Orbit, and Astra implementation remains deferred.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user explicitly activates Venus after the Orbit governance handoff.
2. Every implementation Bead follows the Execution baseline, Reference gate, Crate gate when triggered, contract-proof, portability, and closure rules in AGENTS.md.
3. VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 are either proved at exact accepted commits or retain explicit gaps.
4. Venus records the exact consumed Orbit proof revision and reports every boundary gap to Orbit rather than adding a second terminal or protocol owner.
5. The first client proves one useful Linux window, semantic interaction, reconnect, and bounded failure UX without expanding into workspace features.
6. No known P0 or P1 correctness risk remains unrecorded at the experiment decision boundary.
notes: External sequencing gate: Orbit orb-9o6 must close before graphical implementation begins. Orbit orb-bi4.4 tracks acceptance of the cross-repository Venus consumer; Venus owns its production code and proof. This epic changes no Orbit contract and does not activate Astra.

title: Choose the minimum Venus backend and composition shape
description: Before any Cargo manifest or graphical implementation, choose the smallest backend, composition, text, and renderer ownership shape that can prove VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 against the accepted Orbit frame contract.
design: Run the required reference gate over the exact Orbit proof, FrankenTUI's presenter-emission, terminal-backend, and backend-strategy ADRs plus deterministic backend and test surfaces, OpenTUI Rust's composition model, Ghostling, and libghostty-rs. Then run the crate gate over complete credible shapes: winit plus wgpu and glyphon or cosmic-text; a compatible libghostty-derived renderer boundary; Sugarloaf only if a named need activates it; another maintained native stack found in the gate; and the smallest credible owned or no-new-dependency shape. Compare backend ownership, deterministic patch/damage inputs, Unicode and graphemes, cursor, clipping and layering, native input, accessibility, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, browser implications, owned LOC, dependency/build/Nix cost, maintenance, license, and security. Stop for user choice before a manifest edit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline states that this is a research and dependency decision and changes no product contract by itself.
2. The Reference gate records exact identities and evidence from Orbit, FrankenTUI, OpenTUI Rust, Ghostling, and libghostty-rs before code-shape selection.
3. FrankenTUI is used only for backend, deterministic patch-stream, and test-architecture lessons; OpenTUI Rust only for composition-model lessons; rejected TUI, widget, terminal-output, runtime, and copied-source scope is explicit.
4. The Crate gate compares complete credible ownership shapes, including the smallest owned or no-new-dependency shape where credible, with exact versions and measured or focused evidence.
5. Nonstandard license restrictions are recorded and incompatible reuse or dependencies are rejected.
6. The decision recommends one shape with owner boundaries, expected owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, first contract check, migration risk, and rollback condition.
7. No Cargo manifest, production renderer, compatibility layer, or general UI framework is added before explicit user approval.
notes: Required routing: docs/REFERENCES.md#required-before-the-first-client-implementation. The first proof should expose deterministic frame-to-draw inputs through a headless boundary before manual window dogfood. This Bead does not select a crate merely by naming it.

title: Render one accepted Orbit session in a minimum Linux window
description: Implement the smallest Venus slice: one Linux window consumes canonical structured frames from an already-running Orbit session, renders their accepted rich state, sends semantic input and resize, remains transient across client exit, and explains bounded attachment or server failure.
design: Begin only after the user accepts the backend/composition decision and activates this implementation frontier. Pin the exact accepted Orbit commit and ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 contract states. Before manual window dogfood, use a bounded canonical frame corpus or smallest protocol-faithful source to prove deterministic decode and frame-to-draw inputs without a live PTY, handwritten mirror schema, raw VT parser, or second terminal authority. Keep Linux window and GPU mechanics inside Venus and report any protocol gap to Orbit through separate owner commits and compatibility sequencing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user activates Venus, Orbit orb-9o6 is closed, and the accepted backend/composition decision is recorded before implementation.
2. The Execution baseline records the exact Orbit proof commit, consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states, affected VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 contracts, intended surfaces, and pre-existing worktree state.
3. The pre-code Reference gate and accepted Crate gate satisfy AGENTS.md; manifest changes match the user's exact dependency approval.
4. A focused nonvisual check consumes the canonical Orbit representation and deterministically produces bounded draw inputs for styled Unicode and graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, revisions, and failure cases.
5. One Linux window attaches to an already-running Orbit session, renders coherent complete frames and later revisions, and sends semantic keyboard input and resize through Orbit.
6. Closing or crashing Venus leaves Orbit and the PTY alive; reopening receives coherent current state.
7. Attach rejection, incompatible or invalid frames, and Orbit loss produce clear bounded failures rather than hangs or invented state.
8. Venus owns no PTY, terminal emulator, terminal query response, raw VT parser, mirrored protocol schema, workspace topology, or Astra policy.
9. Closure records deterministic checks, manual visual dogfood, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, exact Orbit compatibility, proof revisions, and remaining gaps.
10. Tabs, panes, sidebars, popups, settings, effects, configuration, plugins, remote/web access, macOS implementation, packaging, and distribution remain excluded.
notes: Required references and classifications are in docs/REFERENCES.md. Orbit orb-bi4.4 is the cross-repository acceptance tracker; this Bead is the sole owner of Venus implementation. A required new Orbit trace format, command, package, adapter, or compatibility window returns for explicit user choice.
